idiom_name: hand-written pthread worker pool over a mutex/condvar job queue (libdispatch where available)
implementation_notes: C offers only the primitives: the dispatcher is a hand-written loop that locks a mutex, takes one job from a bounded queue and signals a condition variable, and the performers are pthread_create() workers that block in pthread_cond_wait() until a job appears. Thread creation can fail with EAGAIN at the process/thread limit, so the pool is created once and the queue must be bounded. On BSD/macOS, libdispatch is the library-grade form: dispatch_async() onto a global concurrent queue schedules each message on the system's thread pool and a serial queue gives a single ordered performer. Keep the pthread form when only POSIX is guaranteed or the dispatch policy must inspect each job before choosing a worker.
pitfalls: pthread_create() fails with EAGAIN once RLIMIT_NPROC / threads-max is reached; a thread per message turns a traffic spike into failed dispatch.
Threads are joinable by default: workers that end without pthread_join() leak their stacks and exit status, so the pool must be joined on shutdown.
A condition-variable wait without a predicate loop re-arms after spurious wakeups and lost signals; always re-check the queue state under the mutex.
Unbounded queue depth plus a mutex-protected queue is a memory-exhaustion path; use a fixed ring buffer and decide whether the dispatcher blocks, rejects or drops.
